summary: Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and under Kosho Uchiyama. He served at Kyoto Soto Zen Center, Minnesota Zen Meditation Center, and as director of the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).
Shoichi Ozawa (1929–2012) worked in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from around 1949 to 1952 and held a post at The Open University of Japan.

Shoji Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University and under Giyu Nishi. He held posts at The Okurayama Institute and served as associate professor and professor at Toyo University (c. 1978–2009).

Shoji Muramoto works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Zurich. His career includes posts at Hanazono University and as Professor of Foreign Studies at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (attested 2002–2009).
Shoju Inaba (1915–1990) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Nagoya University as a part-time lecturer and at Otani University as a professor from circa 1956 to 1985.
Shojun Bando (1932–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1951–1955) and held posts at Otani University and Ueno Gakuen University (c. 1970–2000).

Shokin Furuta (1911–2001) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Matsue High School, Shimane University, University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Education, and under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He held professorships at Hokkaido University and Nihon University.
Shoko Kanaoka (1930–2004) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Toyo University, where he is attested in 1987 and 2000.

Shoko Miyabayashi (1932–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his undergraduate and master's studies at Taisho University, where he subsequently served as lecturer, assistant professor, and dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).

Shoko Miyata works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Miyata holds lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, both attested in 2026.
Shoko Takeuchi (1910–1999) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University and later served there as professor emeritus (attested 1987–1995).

Shoko Watanabe (1907–1977) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Toyo University, and under Naoshiro Tsuji and Ernst Leumann. He held posts at Taisho, Kyushu, and Toyo universities.

Shoku Bando is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg. In 1987, he was affiliated with Kyoto University, Fukui Prefectural College, and Abhidharma Institute.

Shoryu Katsura works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held posts at Toronto, UC Berkeley, Hiroshima University (1976–2004), and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara (1907–1975) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Horyuji Kangakuin, Otani University, and under Susumu Yamaguchi and Join Saeki. He held posts at Doho University, Otani Senshu Gakuin, Otani University, and Otani University Junior College.

Shoshin Ichishima is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a visiting lecturer at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. At Taisho University, he served as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and later Professor Emeritus (attested 2014).

Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1966), where he later served as Assistant Professor and Professor Emeritus at the Institute for Research in the Humanities.

Shoshun Hayashidera is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Posts include the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and Professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Shoson Miyamoto (1893–1983) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, University of Tokyo, and University of Oxford. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Toyo University, Waseda University, and Komazawa University.

Shou-chien Shih is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied as a PhD student at National Sun Yat-sen University, was a professor at National Taiwan University (c. 1990–2006), and served as director of the National Palace Museum (c. 2000–2004).
